concern_details.detail: How do these parts collaborate to provide the main system functionalities?
concern_details.why: The layered Boundary -> Control -> Entity -> Database -> MySQL chain is clear, and it is shown for sign-in, report creation and status update. But the status-update flow, which is the most important collaboration for an architect, is misdrawn. The view folds it into one Control->Entity message, 'update status and notify citizen', with one 'write in transaction'. In the code, Control drives two separate Entity interactions. ReportStatusUpdateController.applyNewStatus calls ReportService.updateReportStatus. requestNotification then goes through NotificationController.verifyNotifiableStatus, which calls ReportService.verifyNotifiableStatus and then generateStatusChangeNotification. So the decision to notify is made in Control, not in Entity, and the update and the notification are two separate PersistenceService transactions (update at ReportService:298, save at :398). The status flow also has no rejection path, although the code rejects non-operators, unknown reports and resolved reports (ReportStatusUpdateController:32-51). Sign-in shows no reply from Control to Boundary, so the 'dashboard or error' outcome has no visible source. The flow that closes the loop, where the operator reviews received reports, is only mentioned in the README and not drawn.

level_why: For an overview, layer-level lifelines plus the user and the external MySQL are appropriate, and three representative flows are a sensible amount. No classes, facade or forms are drawn. Nothing needs to be cut. The changes needed are corrections within the same level, not more detail. Showing the two Control->Entity calls in the status flow keeps the same lifelines.
unsupported: Status-update flow: one 'update report, save notification' message followed by one 'write in transaction'. The code runs two independent transactions: PersistenceService.update(report) in ReportService.updateReportStatus (:298), then PersistenceService.save(notification) in ReportService.generateStatusChangeNotification (:398). Each call begins and commits its own transaction (PersistenceService:34-36, :61-63).

The note placing the 'notifiable status' decision in Entity. In the code, Control decides: NotificationController.verifyNotifiableStatus asks ReportService.verifyNotifiableStatus and only then calls sendNotificationToCitizen -> generateStatusChangeNotification.

Control->Entity message 'update status and notify citizen' as one call. No single domain operation does both. They are separate Control-initiated calls (ReportStatusUpdateController.applyNewStatus and requestNotification).
missing: In the status flow, Control's second interaction with Entity for the notification (check notifiable status, then generate the notification), shown as an opt fragment [status notifiable] on the Control lifeline.

The rejection path in the status update ([not operator / report not found / already resolved] -> error to Boundary), matching what the creation flow already shows (ReportStatusUpdateController:32-51; ReportStatusUpdateGUI catches the exception).

Return messages in sign-in (Database/Entity -> Control 'user session data', Control -> Boundary 'session data or null'), so that the 'dashboard or error' outcome is grounded (UserLoginGUI.sendLoginData:170-180).
uml: The conditional notification is expressed in a note. It should be an 'opt [status notifiable]' combined fragment, as the alt in the creation flow already does.

Lifelines stand for whole layers/packages rather than instances of classifiers. This is acceptable as an overview abstraction, but the README should state it, or the lifelines could be named as role:Layer, e.g. ':Control'.
The sign-in synchronous call chain has no reply messages, while the other flows do. Synchronous calls whose results drive the outcome should show their returns consistently.
fixes: Split the status-update flow into the two Control->Entity calls that exist in the code: 'apply new status' (Entity -> Database 'update report' -> MySQL transaction), then an opt [status notifiable] where Control asks Entity to check and generate the notification (Entity -> Database 'save notification' -> MySQL, a separate transaction).
Replace the note with the opt fragment and put the notifiable-status decision on Control, not Entity.
Add an alt to the status update for the rejection path (not operator / report missing / already resolved -> error shown to the user).
Add the Control -> Boundary reply in sign-in ('session data or none') so that the dashboard-or-error outcome follows from the drawn interaction.
Fix the 'four layers' wording or keep it consistent with the six lifelines, and state in the README that lifelines represent layers (overview abstraction).
